title: Streaming & Suspense: the response as a stream
objectives: Explain how a streamed App Router response is delivered: the shell and Suspense fallbacks first, each boundary's content later in the same response
Place `loading.tsx` or `<Suspense>` for a page, and predict which `await` blocks the whole route and which blocks one section
Predict the status code when `notFound()` or `redirect()` runs after streaming has started, and move the check before anything streams
Explain Partial Prerendering under Cache Components: the prerendered shell, dynamic holes, and the blocking-route error for uncached data outside `<Suspense>`
Spot the layers that buffer a stream (nginx, compression, curl, the platform) and verify chunk timing with a stream reader

sources.title: Next.js docs: Caching (how rendering works, PPR)

questions.prompt: A product page awaits `getProduct()` (80 ms) and then `getRecommendations()` (2.5 s) at the top of `page.tsx`, before returning both sections. How do you get the product on screen while recommendations load?

options.text: Move the recommendations call into its own async component and wrap it in `<Suspense>`
Add `loading.tsx` to the folder
Run both calls with `Promise.all`
Make the page a Client Component and fetch recommendations in `useEffect`

questions.explanation: An `await` blocks everything after it in its component, so the JSX holding any boundary doesn't exist until 2.5 s have passed. Moving the call into a child under `<Suspense>` lets the product render while that one section waits. `loading.tsx` shows a skeleton **instead of** the product, `Promise.all` still waits for the slowest call, and `useEffect` gives up server rendering of that data for a client waterfall.

questions.prompt: `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` does `const user = await getUser((await cookies()).get("session")?.value)`. The folder also has `loading.tsx`. Without Cache Components, what happens when someone navigates to `/dashboard`?

options.text: Navigation waits for the layout: `loading.tsx` wraps the page, not the layout in the same segment
The `loading.tsx` skeleton shows at once while the layout loads
The page renders first and the layout streams in around it
It fails to build, because layouts can't read cookies

questions.explanation: `loading.tsx` becomes a `<Suspense>` **inside** the layout, around the page. Nothing sits above the layout's own `await`, so nothing can be shown until it finishes. The docs' fix: move the data into the page, or wrap the request-time read in its own `<Suspense>` inside the layout. Under Cache Components the same layout is a build error, which forces that fix.

questions.prompt: Three panels resolve at 200 ms, 1 s and 3 s. They're wrapped in **one** `<Suspense>` boundary. When does the user see the 200 ms panel?

options.text: At about 3 s: a boundary shows its content only when everything inside it is ready
At 200 ms: each component streams as soon as it resolves
At 1 s, once a majority of the boundary is ready
Never: one boundary can hold only one async component

questions.explanation: A Suspense boundary swaps its fallback for its children together. Give each panel its own sibling boundary and each appears as soon as its own data arrives, in whatever order. Nesting is for a deliberate sequence (details, then reviews); siblings are for independent panels.

questions.prompt: `app/posts/[slug]/` has `loading.tsx`, and `page.tsx` does `const post = await getPost(slug); if (!post) notFound();`. What status does a request for a missing slug get?

options.text: 200, with the not-found UI and a `noindex` robots meta tag streamed into the page
404, because `notFound()` always sets the status
500, because `notFound()` threw after the response started
307 to the not-found page

questions.explanation: `loading.tsx` makes the page a boundary, so once `getPost` suspends the fallback streams, and the `200` status goes with that first chunk. A later `notFound()` can only change the HTML: Next adds `noindex` so search engines skip it, but uptime checks and some crawlers see a soft 404. Put a fast existence check above any boundary, or answer 404 from `proxy.ts`.

questions.prompt:
With `cacheComponents: true`, a page has a static `
`, a `` component using `use cache` + `cacheLife("hours")`, and `Loading…

}>` where `UserPrefs` reads `cookies()`. What's in the prerendered shell?

options.text: The header, the cached blog posts, and the "Loading…" fallback
Only the header: anything async is left out of the shell
Everything, including the user's preferences from their cookie
Nothing: one `cookies()` call makes the whole route dynamic

questions.explanation: Under PPR, deterministic output and `use cache` results are rendered at build into the shell; request-time work becomes a hole, represented in the shell by its nearest fallback. `UserPrefs` streams in per request. "One `cookies()` makes everything dynamic" was the all-or-nothing behaviour of stable Next before 16.

questions.prompt: Under Cache Components, a Server Component renders `Math.random()` and is wrapped in `<Suspense>`. What happens at `next build`?

options.text: The build reports an error for the route: call `await connection()` first (a new value per request) or move it into `use cache` (one shared value)
It builds, and each visitor gets a new number because `<Suspense>` makes its children dynamic
It builds, and one number is frozen into the prerendered shell for everyone
It builds, and visitors only ever see the fallback

questions.explanation: `<Suspense>` gives a fallback while async work completes; it doesn't opt anything into request-time rendering, and `Math.random()` is synchronous. Next 16 instruments randomness, the current time and crypto during the prerender and stops with an error that asks you to read request data first (`connection()`) or cache the result. That check exists precisely so a value meant to be per request can't be silently frozen into the shell.

questions.prompt: Streaming works on `next start` locally. Behind your nginx in production, each page arrives in one piece after the slowest boundary. First suspect?

options.text: nginx's response buffering: send `X-Accel-Buffering: no`
`<Suspense>` is disabled in production builds
React streams only in development
Streaming needs HTTP/3

questions.explanation: Any layer that collects chunks before forwarding them undoes streaming, and nginx buffers by default. The Self-Hosting guide sets `X-Accel-Buffering: no` through `next.config` `headers()`. Then check compression (a compressor buffers too) and any load balancer in between, by measuring chunk timing at each hop.

prompts.prompt: Name the file that wraps this folder's page in a Suspense boundary.
prompts.explanation: `loading.tsx` becomes the fallback of a `<Suspense>` around `page.tsx` (and nested layouts below it), not around the `layout.tsx` beside it. Its fallback is prefetched, so navigations show it instantly.

prompts.prompt: Stream the orders panel on its own, with a placeholder until it's ready.
prompts.explanation: Each `<Suspense>` boundary is an independent streaming point: its fallback ships in the first chunk and its content follows when `RecentOrders` resolves, without waiting on any sibling.

prompts.prompt: Read a promise started in a Server Component, inside a Client Component under `<Suspense>`.
code: export function StatsChart({ dataPromise }: { dataPromise: Promise<Stats> }) {
prompts.explanation: The Server Component starts `getStats()` without awaiting and passes the promise down (Promises are serialisable props). `use(promise)` suspends the Client Component until it resolves, so the nearest `<Suspense>` fallback shows meanwhile.

prompts.prompt: Under Cache Components, make this component produce a new ID per request instead of one frozen at build.
prompts.explanation: `connection()` tells Next to wait for a real request before continuing, so the prerender stops there and the component becomes a hole (wrap it in `<Suspense>`). It replaced `unstable_noStore` in Next 15.

prompts.prompt: Tell nginx in front of `next start` not to buffer streamed responses.
prompts.explanation: nginx reads `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the upstream response and passes chunks through as they arrive. This is the Self-Hosting guide's own snippet; load balancers and compressors in the path need checking separately.

snippets.question: What status does the client receive, and what does the server log?
snippets.explanation: The first `res.write` sends the status line and headers along with the first chunk. Setting `statusCode` afterwards changes nothing on the wire, and `setHeader` throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`. This is the constraint behind Next's streamed `notFound()`: once the shell is out, the best it can do is put a `noindex` tag in the HTML.

// a client timestamps each chunk it receives
snippets.question:
When does the client receive "

shell

"?
snippets.answer: After about 1.6 s, together with the rest
snippets.explanation: The gzip stream holds small writes until it has enough input to compress or is flushed, so the whole body leaves at `end()`. Calling `gz.flush()` after each write delivers the shell at ~0 ms and each part ~800 ms apart (both runs measured). Compression on by default is one reason a stream that works in one setup arrives in one piece in another; the Streaming guide checks with `Accept-Encoding: identity`.

snippets.question: With Cache Components, what's in the first chunk, and when does the header appear?
snippets.answer: Only the skeleton; the header appears at about 2 s along with the feed
acceptable: FullPageSkeleton, then header and feed together
snippets.explanation: The prerender walks up from `Feed` to the nearest boundary, and that boundary also contains `Header`, so the whole thing becomes one hole: the shell holds only `FullPageSkeleton`. Move `<Header />` outside the boundary (or give `Feed` its own) and the header ships in the first chunk. A boundary placed too high is valid, just coarse.
